name: Bow Valley Provincial Park — Willow Rock Campground
note: Bow Valley PP, 123 sites: 89 unserviced, 34 power (15 amp); upper power loop takes large units (35+ ft), many pull-through. Mix of FCFS and reservable (90 days). Sewage disposal station, showers, laundry on site. --Claude

name: Bow Valley Provincial Park - Three Sisters Campground
note: 36 unserviced FCFS sites suited to RVs and tents beside the Bow River in Bow Valley PP, 12 km east of Canmore near Dead Man's Flats; pit toilets, hand-pump water, hand boat launch. NOTE: temporarily closed for flood recovery since Jun 2026 'until further notice' — verify it has reopened before relying on it. --Claude

name: Spray Valley Provincial Park - Spray Lakes West Campground
note: Unserviced FCFS sites (about 50-63) along the Spray Lake reservoir in Spray Valley PP, 16 km south of Canmore via the gravel Smith-Dorrien/Spray Trail (Hwy 742); vault toilets, hand-pump (non-potable) water. Larger rigs can navigate the maintained gravel access. Open roughly mid-May to mid-Sep. --Claude

name: Beauvais Lake Provincial Park
note: 87 sites (34 unserviced, 53 power-only) suitable for tents and RVs near Beauvais Lake, ~19 km SW of Pincher Creek; gravel pads, potable water, outhouses. Reservable 90 days out; a winterized section (sites 1-15) stays open FCFS with power in the off-season. --Claude

name: Island Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: 40 unserviced sites in a rustic mountain-valley campground on Island Lake, 14 km W of Coleman in Crowsnest Pass; sites accommodate RVs. First-come, first-served (self-registration, cash/cheque). No potable water. Open May-Oct. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Oldman River Provincial Recreation Area
note: 25 unserviced sites (some reservable, some FCFS; includes pull-throughs) along the Oldman River under mature cottonwoods, ~5 km SW of Fort Macleod. Vault toilets, non-potable water. Open mid-May-Sep. Reservable online. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: St. Mary Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area - St. Mary Upper Campground
note: 16 unserviced sites (mix of FCFS and reservable) on a peninsula above St. Mary Reservoir ~5 km NW of Magrath; most sites have lake views, beach nearby. Open year-round (winter sites FCFS). Non-potable water. Reservable online. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Waterton Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA on Waterton Reservoir, 25 km S then E of Pincher Creek. 25 unserviced tent/RV sites, first-come first-served per Alberta Parks; boat launch, pier, firepits, pit toilets, hand pump (non-potable). Open May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Willow Creek Municipal Park (Willow Creek PP)
note: Reclass: the campground/facility zone of Willow Creek Provincial Park was transferred to the Municipal District of Willow Creek in 2010 and is operated by Stavely Elks Parks (local), so ownership is local, not provincial. 55 gravel-pad drive-in sites for tents and RVs plus 2 group sites; individual sites first-come first-served, group sites reservable. Open ~Apr 15-Oct 31. --Claude

name: Etherington Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA in the Highwood Valley, SW of Longview via Hwy 541 + Forestry Trunk Rd. Main Etherington Creek campground has 54 unserviced sites (most suited to RVs and tents, back-in with a few pull-throughs and doubles) plus 6 walk-in tent sites; hand-pump water, vault toilets, sani-dump/potable water 6 km away at Highwood Junction. Mostly reservable 90 days out with some FCFS self-registration sites. Separate horse camp (Etherington Equestrian) is a distinct facility. --Claude

name: Indian Graves Campground (Indian Graves PRA)
note: South Kananaskis PRA campground off the Cowboy Trail (29 km S of Longview on Hwy 22, 13 km W on Hwy 532), bordered by Johnson and Willow creeks; 38 unserviced sites for RVs and tents (lower loop ~21 sites with creek access) plus 6 equestrian sites. No hookups/power, outhouses, non-potable hand pump. Open mid-May to mid-Oct; some sites now reservable on shop.albertaparks.ca (contractor-managed by Wild Rose Campground Mgmt), rest FCFS. --Claude

name: Maycroft Campground (Maycroft PRA)
note: Open-prairie PRA on the Oldman River along the Cowboy Trail (Hwy 22), ~27 km N of Lundbreck. 10 unserviced RV/tent sites, firepits, vault toilets, non-potable pump; self-registration, first-come first-served (14-day max). Popular Oldman River fly-fishing access. --Claude

name: Racehorse Campground (Racehorse PRA)
note: PRA campground 25 km N of Crowsnest on the Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 940), in open pine forest with Racehorse Creek alongside. Sites suitable for RVs and tents; first-come, first-served with self-registration (cash/cheque), non-potable pump, no firewood. Access roads to nearby OHV trails. --Claude

name: Paddy's Flat Campground (Elbow River PRA)
note: ~100 well-treed drive-in sites on 4 loops in the Elbow River valley, 13 km W of Bragg Creek on Hwy 66 (Kananaskis); suits RVs and tents with pull-through sites, water hand pump, toilets, playground, boat launch and river fishing. Several sites back onto the Elbow River. New for 2026: a mix of reservable and first-come, first-served sites (reserve at Shop.AlbertaParks.ca). Open May 1-Oct 31. --Claude

name: Payne Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: 46 unserviced drive-in sites (no hookups) on Payne Lake, 25 km W of Cardston on Hwy 5 (18 km E of Waterton); mix of reservable and first-come, first-served, with pit toilets, boat launch and firewood for sale. Some sites are lakeside or a short walk from the shore. A section stays open FCFS in the off-season. --Claude

name: Lake McGregor Provincial Recreation Area
note: ~100 unserviced drive-in sites (RV and tent) along the Lake McGregor reservoir, just W of the Village of Milo; first-come, first-served, with fire pits, dry toilets, boat launch and garbage bins. Water from a hand pump is not potable-bring drinking water. Open May 1 to October. Provincial recreation area (operated locally by the Village of Milo). --Claude

name: Writing-on-Stone Provincial Park Campground
note: 61 drive-in sites (47 powered year-round, 15/30-amp) in the Milk River valley among the hoodoos at Writing-on-Stone / Aisinai'pi PP (UNESCO World Heritage Site); showers and flush toilets. Reservations mandatory in high season (May long weekend through Sept long weekend); powered sites available FCFS off-season. --Claude

name: Crimson Lake Provincial Park — Crimson Lake Campground
note: Large Alberta Parks campground W of Rocky Mountain House; 161 sites in six loops, RV/trailer-suitable to ~60 ft. 15/30-amp power at all sites, no water/sewer hookups, potable spigots + dump station; modern restrooms, laundry. Mix of reservable and FCFS; 11 powered sites open in winter. --Claude

name: Kootenay Plains Provincial Recreation Area — Two O'Clock Creek Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground on the David Thompson (Hwy 11) corridor ~67 km W of Nordegg. Unserviced sites suitable for RVs (most in open grassland, a few beside Two O'Clock Creek) plus walk-in sites; no hookups; hand-pump water (not potable); no cell service. Mix of reservable and FCFS. North Saskatchewan River a short walk south. --Claude

name: Thompson Creek Provincial Recreation Area — Thompson Creek Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground on the North Saskatchewan River along Hwy 11 near the Banff NP boundary. 50+ well-treed unserviced sites suitable for RVs and tents; no hookups. Partly reservable; note FCFS sites 34–56 were closed due to flooding/bridge safety (check status before relying on them). --Claude

name: Wolf Lake West Campground
note: Remote Alberta Parks auto-access campground on Wolf Lake, ~20 km E of Edson then ~53 km S on Wolf Lake Rd. 36 unserviced sites (some closed after past wildfire), first-come, first-served - no reservations. Boat launch, fish-cleaning stations, vault toilets, non-potable hand pump (bring drinking water). Open ~mid-May-late Sept. --Claude

name: Beaverdam Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small FCFS provincial forest campground on Shunda Creek ~5 km east of Nordegg off Hwy 11. 10 sites: 7 walk-in tent + 3 vehicle pull-up sites for smaller trailers/truck campers (open cleared loops on satellite fit a 23-ft rig), all unserviced; firepits, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Brazeau River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small treed FCFS provincial campground along the Brazeau River, 72 km north of Nordegg on Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734); managed by West Fraser Mills. 7 unserviced drive-in sites, cook shelter, firepits, free firewood, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Brown Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small treed FCFS provincial campground 45 km north of Nordegg on Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734); managed by West Fraser Mills. 7-8 unserviced drive-in sites, firepits, free firewood, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Burnt Timber Provincial Recreation Area
note: FCFS provincial campground on Burnt Timber Creek, ~70 km north of Hwy 1A on Hwy 40 near Water Valley. ~28-30 sites, vehicle-access drive-in on the north side of the creek plus some walk-in tent sites, all unserviced; firepits, picnic tables, pit toilets; bring own drinking water (hand-pump water not potable). Open ~May-Sep. --Claude

name: Chambers Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: FCFS provincial campground near Chambers Creek, west of Rocky Mountain House off Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734). About 25 unserviced drive-in sites, firepits, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Crescent Falls Provincial Recreation Area
note: Well-treed provincial campground above the Bighorn River near Crescent Falls, 22 km west of Nordegg off Hwy 11 then 6 km gravel. ~29 sites: ~20 unserviced vehicle/drive-in + 9 walk-in tent; firepits, pit toilets, no potable water, no cell service. Mix of first-come, first-served and reservable sites. --Claude

name: Dry Haven Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small FCFS provincial campground 11 km west of Nordegg on Hwy 11. 14 unserviced drive-in sites, cook shelter, firepits, pit toilets; no water pump on site, bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Elk Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small FCFS provincial campground near the Clearwater River, 65 km southwest of Rocky Mountain House on Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734); self-maintained by Friends of the Eastern Slopes (FOESA), no nightly fee (membership support encouraged). 13 unserviced drive-in sites, firepits, pit toilets; pack out garbage, bring own drinking water, no firewood collection. OHV off-loading permitted. --Claude

name: Fairfax Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA ~50 km SE of Robb off Hwy 40. 27 spacious unserviced sites in forest near Fairfax Lake (stocked with rainbow trout); boat launch, pier, fish-cleaning stand, firepits, free firewood, pit toilets (hand-pump water not potable). Mix of reservable and FCFS sites; operated for Alberta Parks under FMA contract (West Fraser Mills), still provincial land. --Claude

name: Fallen Timber South Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA (Kananaskis region) ~52 km N of Cochrane via Hwy 1A and Hwy 40. 62 unserviced sites for RVs and tents, shaded and well-spaced, several near Fallen Timber Creek; firepits, pit toilets, hand pump (non-potable). OHV/snowmobile off-loading permitted. Mix of FCFS and reservable sites (reservations via contractor Red Rock Sawmills); provincial land. --Claude

name: McLeod River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA 23 km SE of Hinton via the Robb Rd, along the McLeod River near the Gregg/McLeod confluence. Unserviced treed sites in a northern and southern loop; complimentary firewood, hand-pump water (non-potable, bring your own), pit toilets. Mix of reservable (online ABPP + phone) and first-come, first-served; open mid-May to end of October. --Claude

name: Pembina Forks Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA 63 km SE of Robb on Hwy 40, along the Pembina River. 20 large, well-spaced unserviced spruce-treed sites; firepits, complimentary firewood, vault toilets, hand-pump water. Reservable by phone with some first-come, first-served sites; open May to October. --Claude

name: Prairie Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA ~30 min SW of Rocky Mountain House (near Hwy 752), Caroline area. 50 unserviced mature-forest sites including a number of pull-throughs; water, dry toilets, picnic tables, community kitchen (no firewood on site). Reservable online (ABPP) plus FCFS; dark-sky stargazing. --Claude

name: Ram Falls Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park ~65 km S of Nordegg via gravel Hwy 40/734 (forestry trunk road -- winding, logging trucks, free-range cattle; gravel can be rough in places but passable by a normal vehicle). ~54 unserviced sites in one loop; vault toilets, non-potable water pumps, no firewood. Mix of first-come, first-served and reservable online (ABPP). Ram Falls viewing platform a short walk from camp; limited cell reception. --Claude

name: Seven Mile Campground (Seven Mile Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA in the Clearwater River valley, 48 km SW of Caroline on Hwy 591. 36 unserviced drive-in sites (RV+tent), cook shelter, firepits, pit toilets; bring your own water. First-come, first-served — no reservations (self-managed by Friends of the Eastern Slopes Association; $30 annual membership encouraged). OHV staging area; used by hikers and horseback riders but has no equestrian facilities. Bear country. --Claude

name: Watson Creek Campground (Watson Creek Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA at the confluence of Watson Creek and the McLeod River, ~38 km SW of Robb on a gravel road. ~38 well-treed drive-in sites (RVs and tents), a few next to the McLeod River; free firewood, pit toilets, bring your own water. First-come, first-served ($15 senior); operated by West Fraser Mills under Alberta Parks. Rainbow/bull trout and whitefish fishing. --Claude

name: Whitehorse Creek Campground (Whitehorse Creek Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA and staging area for Whitehorse Wildland PP, ~6 km SW of Cadomin on a gravel access road, along Whitehorse Creek near its confluence with the McLeod River. 26 unserviced drive-in sites (17 general + 9 equestrian with corrals/pens/tie stalls); firepits, free firewood, pit toilets, hand-pump water. Reservations recommended (equestrian sites by phone; one FCFS site); operated by West Fraser Mills; season May-Oct. General campground that also offers horse sites. --Claude

name: Miquelon Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park ~68 km SE of Edmonton. Miquelon Lake campground has 269 sites (82 unserviced, 187 powered 15/30A) across A/B/C areas, showers, flush toilets, two dump stations. Reservable May-Oct via reservation.albertaparks.ca; a handful of Loop A sites are winter FCFS. Suited to tents and RVs. --Claude

name: Jarvis Bay Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park 4 km N of Sylvan Lake off Hwy 20. Main campground ~193 sites, virtually all powered (15/30A), well-treed with drive-through sites accommodating large RVs; a separate North Loop is tent-only. Reservable May-Sep (sites 186-195 add FCFS after early Sep). Showers, flush toilets, RV fill station. --Claude
